regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Cypress Mountain is forecast for about 61". Whistler follows.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Crystal Mountain is forecast for about 48", 30" of it Thursday. Mt. Baker and Mt. Bachelor follow.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Grand Targhee is forecast for about 25". Jackson Hole and Sun Valley follow.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Palisades is forecast for about 18". Kirkwood and Sugar Bowl follow. The NWS is calling for more at Kirkwood: 9 to 19 inches Sunday through Wednesday night.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Killington is forecast for about 15", all of it Thursday. Stowe and Jay Peak follow.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: RED Mountain is forecast for about 14", 9" of it Thursday. Whitewater and Revelstoke follow.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: Brighton is forecast for about 12", 6" of it Thursday. Solitude and Snowbasin follow.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Sun Peaks is forecast for about 10", 7" of it Thursday. SilverStar and Big White follow.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Telluride is forecast for about 8", 4" of it Saturday. Aspen Highlands and Vail follow.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Taos is forecast for about 6", 3" of it Saturday. Wolf Creek follows.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
